before:
Fell Pony Grazing Trust — Warden's Handbook, Section 5

Where applications for summer grazing exceed the allowance carried by the common, the warden settles them in a fixed order. Length of continuous membership is taken first, then distance of the holding from the gate, and a drawn ballot only where those two leave a tie. No applicant is excluded by this exercise, and every applicant remains free to graze the winter enclosure, to sub-let a stint with written consent, or to withdraw before the turn-out date. Wardens should note that the order set out above governs only who is served first when the allowance runs short, and that the total number of stints released each year is settled elsewhere in this handbook.

before:
Tidal Mill — Sluice Keeper's Log, Standing Entries

The keeper enters the state of the pond, the wind, and the hour of every gate movement at the head of each shift. Standing entries are repeated at the front of the book. The lower gate may be opened by the keeper working alone during daylight, provided the pond stands below the marked stone. The upper gate is never worked without a second person on the walkway. Visitors are kept behind the chain while any gate is in motion. Where the pond stands above the marked stone, the keeper waits for the ebb and enters the delay against the shift, together with the hour of the next inspection.
after:

Visitors are kept behind the chain while any gate is in motion. before:
Estuary Gauge Network — Station 7 Configuration Note

Station 7 sits on the outer wall of the old ferry steps and reports at six-minute intervals to the county server. The datum offset applied to every reading from this station is 2.14 metres, and the figure is confirmed by the levelling run of the previous winter, so reported heights may be used directly. The logger clock is disciplined nightly against the network signal. Battery exchange falls in the first week of each quarter and the desiccant sachet is renewed at the same visit. Anyone amending the offset field must leave the previous value commented out beneath it, with the date of the change and the initials of the technician who made it.

before:
Brickworks — Green Ware Drying Manual, Part 3

Drying hours for each barrow load are set before the load enters the shed. The setter derives the figure from the works' own moisture curve, taking the wet weight at the bench and reading the hours off the curve pinned beside the door. The figure is chalked on the load ticket and the ticket travels with the barrow. Nothing here alters who may set a load, the maximum shed temperature, or the requirement that every load be turned once. Loads exceeding the chalked hours by more than a shift are reported to the foreman. The shed thermometer is read at the start and end of each shift and entered on the sheet.
after:

before:
Inshore Weather Bulletin — Volunteer Observers' Note

Observers post one line to the shared board at each of the three daily reading times. The line carries the station letter, the wind force, the visibility band, the sea state and the hour, with the fields separated by commas and no spaces after them. The board is scraped every hour by the county collator, and a line that cannot be split is dropped without warning to the observer. Nothing here changes what is observed, or how often. Observers who miss a reading time leave the slot empty rather than posting a late line, and note the omission in the monthly return sent to the collator.

before:
Toolshare Catalogue — Front Matter

Throughout this catalogue an item counts as one loan unit if it can be carried in one hand by a single borrower. The per-member limit of four units, the deposit bands in Appendix B, the shelf numbering and the annual stock count are all worked out from that one test, so any alteration to it moves every figure in the book. Sets kept together but failing the test are entered as several units and shelved apart. Members are asked to return units to the shelf position printed on the tag. The catalogue is reprinted each January, and the previous printing is kept in the office for reference.
